questions.question: A new car costs Rs. 1280000. In the first year its value drops by 25 percent. What is it worth at the end of the first year?
questions.solution:
**Data:**

Initial cost of car = Rs. 1280000,

Depreciation in the first year = 25%.

**Concept:**

Depreciation is the decrease in the value of an asset over time.

**Solution:**

Value of car at the end of first year: 1280000 - (25/100) × 1280000 = Rs. 960000.

**Therefore, the car is worth Rs. 960000 at the end of the first year.**

questions.question: An item costing Rs. 500 is being sold at a 17% loss. If the price is further reduced by 20%, then find the selling price.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) = Rs. 500

Loss Percentage = 17%

Further reduction = 20%

**Formula Used:**

Selling Price (SP) = Cost Price (CP) - Loss

Further Reduced Price = SP - (20% of SP)

**Calculation:**

Loss = 17% of CP

⇒ Loss = 17/100 × 500

⇒ Loss = 85

Selling Price (SP) = CP - Loss

⇒ SP = 500 - 85

⇒ SP = 415

Further Reduction = 20% of SP

⇒ Further Reduction = 20/100 × 415

⇒ Further Reduction = 83

Further Reduced Price = SP - Further Reduction

⇒ Further Reduced Price = 415 - 83

⇒ Further Reduced Price = 332

**The selling price after further reduction is Rs. 332.**

questions.question: P sells a laptop to Q at a profit of 50 percent and Q sells it to R at a profit of 60 percent. What is the ratio of cost prices of P and R?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

P sells a laptop to Q at a profit of 50 percent.

Q sells it to R at a profit of 60 percent.

**Formula Used:**

Cost PriceQ = Selling PriceP

Selling Price = Cost Price + Profit

Ratio = CPP / CPR

**Calculation:**

Let the cost price of the laptop for P be CPP = 100.

Selling PriceP = CPP + 50% of CPP

Selling PriceP = 100 + (50/100) × 100

Selling PriceP = 100 + 50

Selling PriceP = 150

Now, CPQ = Selling PriceP = 150

Selling PriceQ = CPQ + 60% of CPQ

Selling PriceQ = 150 + (60/100) × 150

Selling PriceQ = 150 + 90

Selling PriceQ = 240

Now, CPR = Selling PriceQ = 240

Ratio of CPP to CPR:

Ratio = CPP / CPR

Ratio = 100 / 240

⇒ Ratio = 5 / 12

**The ratio of cost prices of P and R is 5 ∶ 12.**

questions.question: Ritu sold a camera for ₹24000, earning a profit of 20%. If she wanted to earn a profit of 25%, at what price should she have sold the camera?
questions.solution:

**Solution:**

24000 = CP × (120/100)

questions.question: The profit earned on selling a bike for ₹ 68,250 is the same as the loss incurred on selling the bike for ₹ 47,250. Find the cost price of the bike.
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When the profit earned on selling an article is exactly equal to the loss incurred, the Cost Price (CP) is simply the average of the two selling prices.

CP = (SP₁ + SP₂) ÷ 2

CP = (68250 + 47250) ÷ 2

CP = 115500 ÷ 2 = 57750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 57,750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Selling Price with profit (SP₁) = ₹ 68,250

Selling Price with loss (SP₂) = ₹ 47,250

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4583e1dea2de780f3534e02f43013abc191003ff65c221c28fff763d0b860f72.png] 

**Formula Used:**

Profit = SP − CP

Loss = CP − SP

**Calculation:**

⇒ Profit = Loss

⇒ 68250 − CP = CP − 47250

⇒ CP + CP = 68250 + 47250

⇒ 2 × CP = 115500

⇒ CP = 115500 ÷ 2

⇒ CP = 57750

**∴ The correct answer is ₹ 57,750.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Cost Price (CP) & Selling Price (SP)

When an article is sold at a gain, SP > CP. The difference is Profit = SP − CP. When it is sold at a loss, CP > SP. The difference is Loss = CP − SP.

When Profit equals Loss

If the profit made by selling an article at SP₁ is exactly equal to the loss incurred by selling it at SP₂, then the Cost Price (CP) is the arithmetic mean of the two selling prices. CP = (SP₁ + SP₂) ÷ 2.

Profit and Loss Percentage

Both profit and loss percentages are always calculated on the Cost Price (CP) unless specifically stated otherwise. Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100.

questions.question: Rohit buys an old bat for Rs. 2320 and spends Rs. 180 on its repairing. If he sells it for Rs. 2400, then what is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Cost price of the old bat = Rs. 2320

Repairing cost = Rs. 180

Selling price = Rs. 2400

**Formula Used:**

Loss Percentage = (Loss / Cost Price) × 100

**Calculation:**

Total Cost Price = Rs. 2320 + Rs. 180 = Rs. 2500

Loss = Total Cost Price - Selling Price

⇒ Loss = Rs. 2500 - Rs. 2400

⇒ Loss = Rs. 100

Loss Percentage = (Loss / Cost Price) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = (100 / 2500) × 100

⇒ Loss Percentage = 4%

**The loss percentage is 4%.**

questions.question: The difference between cost price and selling price of a table is Rs. 224. If loss percentage is 40 percent, then what is the selling price?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Difference between Cost Price (CP) and Selling Price (SP) = Rs. 224

Loss Percentage = 40%

**Formula used:**

SP = CP × (1 - Loss Percentage / 100)

**Calculations:**

SP = CP × (1 - 0.40)

⇒ SP = CP × 0.60

CP - SP = 224

⇒ CP - (CP × 0.60) = 224

⇒ CP × (1 - 0.60) = 224

⇒ CP × 0.40 = 224

⇒ CP = 224 / 0.40

⇒ CP = 560

⇒ SP = CP × 0.60 = 560 × 0.60

⇒ SP = 336

**∴ The selling price of the table is Rs. 336.**

questions.question: Rohit buys an old bat for Rs. 880 and spends Rs. 120 on its repairing. If he sells it for Rs. 800, then what is the loss percentage?
questions.solution:
**Given**

Cost of old bat = Rs. 880

Repairing cost = Rs. 120

Selling price = Rs. 800

**Concept:**

Loss% = (Loss/CP) × 100%

**Solution:**

⇒ CP = Cost of old bat + Repairing cost = 880 + 120 = Rs. 1000

⇒ Loss = CP - Selling price = 1000 - 800 = Rs. 200

⇒ Loss% = (200/1000) × 100% = 20%

**Therefore, the loss percentage is 20%.**

questions.question: A man purchased two items at the same price and sold one at a profit of 15% and the other at a loss of 5%. If the difference between the two selling prices is ₹80, then what is the cost price of one item?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Difference in selling prices = ₹80

Profit on one item = 15%

Loss on the other item = 5%

**Concept used: **

Profit/loss percentage formula.

**Solution:**

Let the cost price be x.

Selling price of the first item = x + 15% of x = 1.15x

Selling price of the second item = x - 5% of x = 0.95x

The difference in selling prices = 1.15x - 0.95x = 0.2x = ₹80

Solving for x, x = ₹80 / 0.2 = ₹400

**Therefore, the cost price of one item is ₹400.**

questions.question: When the price of an article was reduced by 40% its sale increased by 60%. What was the net effect on the sale?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Reduction in Price = 40%

Increase in Sales = 60%

**Calculations:**

1. Let the original price of the article be P and original sales be S.

2. New Price after Reduction:

⇒ New Price = P × (1 - 0.40) = P × 0.60

3. New Sales after Increase:

⇒ New Sales = S × (1 + 0.60) = S × 1.60

4. Calculate the Original Revenue:

⇒ Original Revenue = P × S

5. Calculate the New Revenue:

⇒ New Revenue = (P × 0.60) × (S × 1.60) = 0.96PS

6. Determine the Change in Revenue:

⇒ Change = New Revenue - Original Revenue = 0.96PS - PS = -0.04PS

7. Percentage Change:

⇒ Percentage Change = (-0.04PS / PS) × 100 = -4%

**∴ The net effect on sales is a decrease of 4%.**

questions.question: If selling price of a table is 25 percent of its cost price, then what is the loss percentage?

**∴ Dinesh's profit is 20%.**

 +32% Profit
 
 132% of CP = SP

Loss Percentage

When a product is sold at a loss, the Cost Price can be calculated using the formula: CP = [100 ÷ (100 − Loss%)] × SP.

Marked Price & Discount

Discount is always calculated on the Marked Price (MP). The relation between Cost Price, Marked Price, Profit% and Discount% is direct: CP × (100 + Profit%) = MP × (100 − Discount%).

Dishonest Dealer

If a seller sells goods at cost price but uses false weights, the profit percentage is calculated as: Profit% = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.

questions.question: Ketan sold 151 chairs and had a gain equal to the selling price of 51 chairs. What is his profit percentage?
questions.solution:
* __Shortcut Trick__

Let SP of 1 chair = 1 unit.

SP of 151 chairs = 151 units, and Gain = 51 units.

CP = Total SP − Gain = 151 − 51 = 100 units.

Profit % = (Gain ÷ CP) × 100 = (51 ÷ 100) × 100 = 51%.

**∴ The correct answer is 51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total chairs sold = 151

Gain = Selling Price of 51 chairs

Cost Price (CP) = Selling Price (SP) − Profit

Profit % = (Profit ÷ CP) × 100

 

 Total Selling Price = 151 units
 
 
 
 
 Cost Price = 100
 Profit = 51

 Profit % = (51 ÷ 100) × 100 = 51%

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let SP of 1 chair = 1 unit.

⇒ Total SP (151 chairs) = 151 units

⇒ Profit (SP of 51 chairs) = 51 units

⇒ CP = SP − Profit = 151 − 51 = 100 units

⇒ Profit % = (51 ÷ 100) × 100

⇒ Profit % = 51%

**∴ The correct answer is 51%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Loss in terms of Selling Price

If loss equals the SP of x* items when selling *y* items, then CP = SP of (*y* + *x*) items. Loss % = [*x* ÷ (*y* + *x*)] × 100.

Gain in terms of Cost Price

If gain equals the CP of *x* items when selling *y* items, then CP is equivalent to *y* items. Profit % = (*x* ÷ *y*) × 100.

Dishonest Dealer Concept

If a dealer sells goods at CP but uses false weight, Profit % = [Error ÷ (True Value − Error)] × 100.
